title: Craft producers file frequent COLA label applications; TTB median turnaround is fast, so evidence for a broad delay problem is insufficient and rework and upcoming label rules remain unmeasured

history.reason: Signal from TTB COLA collection notice and labeling proposed rule.

TTB's own current median processing times are 1-6 days against a 15-day goal and the per-application burden estimate is 31 minutes. This is insufficient evidence for a broad delay thesis; it does not rule out costly delays for a subset (the median is a single snapshot with no tail data) or establish an alternative pain. Rework and the Alcohol Facts rule remain hypotheses. Revisit if the rule is finalized or independent evidence shows large rework, tail delay or consultant cost. Current status: paused.

description: Alcohol producers, bottlers and importers must obtain a Certificate of Label Approval (COLA) for each label before interstate sale; TTB estimates about 213,200 applications a year at 31 minutes each, while its own current data show fast median turnaround. The available sources are insufficient to support a broad delay problem, but they do not exclude delay costs for a subset or show where real pain lies; rework, label-change cost and a proposed Alcohol Facts requirement are unmeasured hypotheses.
customer_segment: Breweries, wineries, distilleries, bottlers and importers that sell across state lines; TTB says the vast majority are small entities (about 99 percent by SBA size standards). Number of small craft producers filing is not established (TTB: fewer than 18,000 applicants over FY 2020-2022).
context: Based on a November 2024 PRA notice, a January 2025 proposed rule and a live TTB page read 2026-11-04. The permit side (TTB permits and recurring excise/operations reports) was not examined here beyond noting TTB publishes separate permit processing times.

evidence.text: TTB estimates 13,000 respondents file an average of 16.4 label applications a year (213,200 responses) at 31 minutes each, for 110,153 burden hours.
TTB received 192,954 label applications in FY 2022 and reports 139,048 received in 2026 to date as of 2026-11-04.
TTB estimates initial compliance with the proposed Alcohol Facts rule at roughly $1,636 per UPC, or about $1,636 to $16,636 for a firm with one to ten UPCs over a proposed 5-year period.
Over a dozen commenters, mostly small producers or trade associations, asked for a small business exemption from new label requirements, according to TTB.
Small producers may spend material time or consultant fees on label compliance review and rejected-application rework beyond the 31-minute form burden.

alternatives: Applying directly in COLAs Online at no fee (TTB states there is no fee).
Compliance consultants, label printers or distributors who check labels: not investigated.

contradictory_evidence.text: TTB's current median label processing times are 1 day (malt beverages), 2 days (wine) and 6 days (distilled spirits) against a 15-day goal. TTB defines processing as median days from receipt until approval or rejection, including correction exchanges; no distribution, tail, rejection rate or resubmission count was shown.

Inference: fast medians suggest slow approval is not a widespread pain, but a single median cannot exclude costly delays for a subset of applicants (for example those with repeated corrections), so this weakens rather than rules out a delay thesis.

TTB's own estimate of 31 minutes per application is small, and TTB certifies the proposed Alcohol Facts rule would not significantly burden a substantial number of small entities; these are agency self-assessments and not measured burden.
TTB's proposal does not require new COLA submissions for Alcohol Facts changes, which would limit paperwork volume if adopted as proposed.
Whether label rejections or resubmissions are common and costly for craft producers was not shown in any source read.

uncertainty: Unknown: rejection and resubmission rates, true producer time and consultant spend per label, how many applicants are small craft producers, whether the Alcohol Facts rule was finalized, and the permit and recurring excise/operations-report burden (not examined). The median turnaround is a single-day snapshot that includes rejected and corrected applications and says nothing about the tail.
open_questions: What share of COLA submissions are rejected or returned, and how long does a correction cycle take?
Was the Alcohol Facts proposal finalized, and with what compliance date?
What do small producers actually pay for label review or consultants?
Is the burden larger in permits and recurring monthly/quarterly reports than in labels?
next_actions: Look for TTB annual report or FOIA data on COLA rejection rates.
Check the status of RIN 1513-AC93 and read the regulations.gov comments from small producers.
Examine TTB permit and operations-report information collections separately.
